subject.title: All LLM API calls time out simultaneously despite APIs being reachable (multi-agent concurrency issue)

question: After the current terminal-abort mitigation, should the next owner treat this as a remaining core concurrency bug, a Telegram runner/concurrency issue, a provider timeout/fallback-budget issue, or an operator-default/documentation issue?
rationale: The issue bundles several plausible fixes across agent fallback policy, Telegram polling, Node launch environment, DNS behavior, and session-lock diagnostics, and choosing the wrong boundary could add compatibility-sensitive config or defaults without fixing the real bottleneck.

options.title: Run live repro first
options.body: Keep the issue open and require a current-main four-agent Telegram/provider repro before choosing the code boundary or adding config/defaults.

options.title: Scope to fallback budgeting
options.body: Treat this as a model-fallback timeout-budget issue and pursue per-candidate/provider timeout behavior after owner approval.

options.title: Scope to Telegram/runtime defaults
options.body: Treat the primary suspect as Telegram runner concurrency or process launch defaults and ask that owner group to design the least disruptive change.

recommendation.title: Run live repro first
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and require a current-main four-agent Telegram/provider repro before choosing the code boundary or adding config/defaults.

likelyOwner.reason: altaywtf most recently accepted and merged adjacent terminal-vs-retryable fallback behavior and provided live provider proof for that boundary.
